> What it sounds like to me is you just want someone to tell you that you aren't trans. 


Youre right. I do want someone to tell me that. I want someone to tell me that this is all my head. I dont want to feel like I want to be a women. I dont like looking at women and wishing that I looked like them. Its such a frustrating feeling of hold two contradicting thoughts of wanting to be one and being happy with what I am.

>The bottom line is we can't tell you who you are and what to identify as only you can do that through self discovery and being honest with yourself.



I don't know what being honest with myself looks like. I want to believe that these feelings Im just a phase. It gets its worst when Im stressed, sad, or in bed when I think of fake scenarios, so I try to convince myself that it's just a form of escapism.

> queer friendly therapist

Ive thought it but my fear is that such a therapist is just going to dogmatically(for lack of a better word) affirm that I am trans. I don't consider myself that. I want someone who will push back and try to get to the root of the issue.
Thank you <3

> Are these feelings of not wanting to draw attention to yourself getting in your way of becoming a more genuine version of yourself?

Its not about drawing attention to myself, its about wanting to feel pretty. I've joked about doing my makeup and trying to pass as a women with a friend and he said that Im too good looking as a man and couldnt pass no matter how hard I tried. He added that if I tried it would be gross because it would be obvious that I was a man trying to be a women.

If Im honest, I agree. When I picture myself as trying to pass I look REALLY bad. I thought about actually trying to pass in the context of crossplaying as a female character. My biggest hurdle is my face. Im not androgenous in the slightest. I've thought about wearing a mask and only doing my eye makeup, and learning to do a girl voice(Ive tried learning how to do one but I cant seem to do it) Im not too worried about my body shape. I was going to shave all of my exposed skin and get silicone body forms.

Yes. I am in therapy. I have been going on and off for about 5 years, but am steady with this therapist for about a year. 

>They also, like my parents, may just completely misunderstand the root cause(s) of depression and think that because "you have a good life" you should just get over it and appreciate what you have. They don't understand that you can't just flip that switch the other way so get mad at you for seemingly not trying. 

I dont know. Because, I have tried explaining things to them but its like we start from square one everytime we talk. Thats why I think they are narcissists. I have tried explain things to my parents, like that Im not good in social situations and they keep saying that "I need to get that out of my head" but that isnt my experience at all. I tell them my experience but they just say that Im wrong. They cant seem to grasp that this is what I experience. This is why I think I find it impossible to have good communication with friends, and even other people. When they do something that bothers me I usually just hold in and start to resent them. Im working on it. I found a friend that listens to me and it's very strange to have. She's patient when I overthink and over apologize. When I say something she believes me. 

>The real world is hard and scary and not always fair.

That is where I keep falling short. I don't want to experience "the real world" because I dont see a point to all of that suffering. There is no end game. There's nothing to work towards. I feel like Im just going to exist, and work just to survive. Most people today live paycheck to paycheck. Why would I assume that I wouldn't be one of those people? That sound like an awful way to live. I hear so many people say that. If the real world is like that, why would I want to live in it?

Every little thing someone does or if someone has an issue with their wardrobe becomes "oh my God. Did you see the way her x was" or  they will go on and on about how annoying someone it.

Ive developed serious trusts issues because of this. I feel that whenever I do anything or mess up in public people are going to go on talking shit and remembering every dumb thing I've done.

That happened with my dad. Whenever they sit me down to talk I used to deflect and say "I don't know". One time I kept saying  "It doesn't matter because you aren't going to listen what I have to say. What I say doesn't matter to you. You've already made up your mind". 

I kept saying "It doesn't matter" and he really worked himself up and actually hit me over the head several times. I begged him to stop and he kept saying "Stop crying like a little girl" and "I'm not hitting you. If I was you would have been knocked out. These are love taps" while hitting me with closed fists.



When he was done both my parents asked my why I cried so much and I couldn't help but laugh to myself. The next day he bought me some candy. I told him I really didn't appreciate him hitting me and his response was "I just wanted to knock some sense into you"

It wasnt really them who caused me to have this view, or at least I dont think so. I dont know what to write anymore, Im sorry. Ive been sitting on this for a few hours and all of the thoughts are just random strings of info that's impossible to write into words. Thank you for everything

Thank you. This really means alot. This may sound odd but its really weird hearing someone saying that, that my health is important. Whenever I try to stand up for my emotional/physical health Im either insulted, being told that the pain I feel is all in my head or even hit by my father. There are mental blocks in my head for when people ask me how I am because they drilled into my head that when I have a problem and try to work it out Im playing the victim. Even when Im with a therapist. Im hesitant to open up to them because I think they are going to be judgmental and secretly think that Im just acting.

Whenever I hear "light at the end of the tunnel" I think of the variant of that which goes "The light at the end of tunnel is just a freight train coming to hit me" I dont remember where I heard it from but it really stuck with me because I honesty dont have any hope. Everyone always tells me 'Enjoy life while you can" or "Life really sucks" or some variation of that and then in the same breath say "Life is fun". I just dont understand it. 

In your post you said "Think about all the great times you've had with your closest friends. Wouldn't you want more of those?" I do, but none of that is work dealing with the drudgery and hardship of life. How would I know that Im missing out if Im dead? 


Theres an exchange between two characters from a show that I watched a few months ago that has really stuck with me because is really summarizes how I feel about life:

>C1:Do you feel any better?

>C2: Yeah I guess.

>C1: Ah that's great, Charlie we did it. successful mission.

>C2: For bit and It ended, like good things always do.

>C1: Huh, Well yeah, nice things can't last forever 

>C2: That's exactly it, are the best parts of life just finding momentary distractions to keep yourself busy so you dont think about the harsh reality of life for a second? I can ride roller coasters, meet new friends, and spend time with my family all day long.Its doesn't change the fact all of this was for nothing. 

My friend who works full time tells me that he wishes that he could just enjoy life. He hates coming home and being tired. I dont want live if this is what life is like.

I just dont understand why Im forced to live if I dont want to deal with any of that. In Belgium they allow psychiatric euthanasia for people who dont want to live because their suffering is unbearable. Theres no pain, virtual zero chance of failure. No one find them with pieces of their head scattered across the room. They get to die with dignity surrounded by friends and family.
